Google Analytics has been one of the most valuable tools I have learned during my marketing coursework. It provides businesses with data about how users find, navigate, and interact with a website. Instead of making decisions based on assumptions, marketers can use real user behavior to improve digital strategies.

::: section-light
## Hands-On Practice with the GA4 Demo Account

Beyond my coursework, I practiced inside Google's official GA4 Demo Account, which connects to real, live data from the Google Merchandise Store, Google's own ecommerce site. Since it uses actual traffic and transaction data rather than sample numbers, it gave me a realistic environment to explore standard reports, build custom explorations, and interpret ecommerce metrics without needing my own live website.

::: card
### What I Explored

- **Acquisition reports** — comparing organic search, paid, direct, and referral traffic to see which channels drove the most engaged users.
- **Engagement reports** — reviewing session duration, engagement rate, and top pages/screens to understand on-site behavior.
- **Monetization and ecommerce reports** — tracking product views, add-to-cart actions, checkout progress, and completed purchases through the full purchase funnel.
- **Explore tab** — building a simple funnel exploration to see where users dropped off between viewing a product and completing checkout.

<div class="button-row">

[Access the GA4 Demo Account](https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/6367342?hl=en){.button target="_blank"}

:::

Working inside a real, high-traffic GA4 property (rather than a small or empty test account) made the reports feel much more meaningful. It also reinforced the certification concepts I had studied, since I could immediately see how metrics like acquisition, engagement, and conversion connect to real purchase behavior.
:::

## Course Reflection

Throughout this course I became much more comfortable using Google Analytics. At the beginning, many of the reports and metrics seemed overwhelming. As I completed more activities, I learned how different reports work together to tell a story about customer behavior.

I also gained a better appreciation for how digital marketers use analytics to improve websites, evaluate campaigns, and support business decisions.
